R.DEVDAS J., (ORAL):
The petitioners, who are the children of late Shri.T.Nagappa, are before this Court with a grievance regarding 10 guntas of land in Sy.No.12/9 of Sarakki Agrahara village, Beguru Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, which forms the petition schedule property.
2. Some of the undisputed facts are that, 2 acres and 9 guntas of land in the said survey number was notified for acquisition in the year 1967 and 1970.
It is not disputed that the said lands were notified and acquired for formation of Sarakki Layout.
It is also not disputed that the petitioners' father sought for enhancement of compensation and received the compensation awarded in respect of lands belonging to the petitioners' father.
However, the dispute is only regarding 10 guntas of land.

In that regard, learned Senior Counsel Shri.Suresh S Lokre, appearing for the petitioners has drawn the attention of this Court to a judgment passed by the City NC: 2023:KHC:29335 Civil Court at Bengaluru, in O.S.No.1922/2003.

entities.text: City NC: 2023:KHC:29335 Civil Court at Bengaluru
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That was a suit filed by one Shri.H.Ramamurthy and others against the Commissioner, Bangalore Development Authority, Shri.T.Nagappa (father of the petitioners, who was arraigned as defendant No.2) and Shri.T.Hanumanthappa, who was the brother of late Shri.T.Nagappa.
The suit was filed for the relief of permanent and mandatory injunction in respect of the very same 10 guntas of land, which is the subject matter of this writ petition.

It was the contention of the plaintiffs that they are the owners of the 10 guntas of land and since the acquisition notifications were not issued in the name of the plaintiffs and no award was declared in favour of the plaintiffs, the defendants have no manner of right, title or interest in respect of the suit schedule property and therefore, the defendants should be permanently restrained from interfering with the suit schedule property.

3. Learned Senior Counsel while taking this Court through the judgment dated 20.08.2009, has pointed out that the respondent-Bangalore Development Authority NC: 2023:KHC:29335 (hereinafter referred to as 'the BDA', for short) has clearly taken a stand in the written statement that as per the mahazar drawn by the revenue authorities of the BDA at Ex.D7, it was found that out of the notified extent of 2 acres and 9 guntas of land, there were malikies like standing trees of different varieties, residential buildings and other structures etc., and as such without disturbing those malikies, more particularly, residential buildings of the owners of the property, the remaining portion of the land has been taken possession.

The judgment refers to page No.2 of the mahazar at Ex.D7 and it was found that there is a specific reference with regard to the existence of the residential buildings and other structures of defendant No.2-Shri.T.Nagappa in an extent of 10 guntas of land notified for acquisition and as such, the 10 guntas of land continued to be in possession of defendant No.2.

sentences.text: 4. Learned Senior Counsel submits that along with a memo dated 23.05.2023, the certified copy of the mahazar dated 11.11.1976, which was marked as Ex.D7 in the suit has been furnished.
Learned Senior Counsel would NC: 2023:KHC:29335 therefore submit that the BDA cannot now take a different stand rescinding from the stand taken before the civil court.

5. Learned Senior Counsel further submits that in the statement of objections filed at the hands of respondent-BDA, several contradictory stands have been taken including, a contention that possession of the petition schedule property was also taken and it is stated in the objections that the mahazar at Ex.D7 is a fake document.

Learned Counsel would submit that this Court should take judicial notice of the contradictory stands now sought to be taken by the BDA, trying to rescind from its admission in the written statement filed before the civil court.

6. Learned Senior Counsel would further submit that the writ petition is not hit by delay and laches,
as is sought to be contended by the respondent-BDA in its statement of objections.

The cause of action arose for the petitioners on 07.11.2014, when the respondents tried to disturb the possession of the petition schedule property NC: 2023:KHC:29335 and bulldozers were brought with the help of the police to take forcible possession of the petition schedule property.
Learned Senior Counsel would therefore submit that there is no substance in the contention of the respondent-BDA that the writ petition is hit by delay and laches.

Learned Senior Counsel would further submit that although several prayers are made in the writ petition including seeking a declaration at the hands of this Court that the scheme has lapsed insofar as the petition schedule property is concerned, the petitioners will restrained their prayer before this Court seeking protection and a direction to the respondent-BDA not to forcibly dispossess the petitioners.

7. Learned Senior Counsel would further submit that when the petitioners have brought to the notice of this Court the stand taken by the BDA in its written statement filed before the civil court and a contrary stand is now sought to be taken, this Court should hold that the BDA cannot now contend that it has taken possession of the petition schedule property and thereafter lawfully allotted the same in favour of respondent No.3-Bangalore Urban NC: 2023:KHC:29335 Employees House Building & Social Welfare Co-operative Society Ltd., (hereinafter referred to as 'the society ',
for short).

sentences.text: Respondent No.3-society is said to have been allotted with 1493.04 sq.mtrs., of land in Sy.No.12/9, as per the allotment letter dated 01.12.2014.

However, it is sought to be contended that the entire property allotted in favour of respondent No.3-society measuring 1493.04 sq.mtrs., were thereafter sold in favour of respondent No.4 under a registered sale deed dated 29.09.2015,
subsequent to the filing of this writ petition.
Therefore, respondent No.4 was subsequently impleaded in this writ petition.

Learned Senior Counsel would therefore submit that the action of respondent-BDA in allotting the property in favour of respondent No.3-society is contrary to the admitted facts that the petition schedule property measuring 10 guntas of land were never taken possession of by the BDA and therefore, the BDA could not have allotted the property in favour of respondent No.3-society.

Moreover, respondent No.4 has purchased the property at the hands of respondent No.3-society and respondent NC: 2023:KHC:29335 No.3-society has disposed of the property during the pendency of the writ petition.
Therefore, neither respondent No.3 nor respondent No.4 could claim any equity.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Counsel Shri.B.S.Sachin appearing for the respondent-BDA submits that while taking this Court through the statement of objections and additional statement of objections that the petitioners cannot deny the fact that the award was passed in respect of the entire 2 acres and 9 guntas of land which were notified and acquired.

Shri.T.Nagappa, the father of the petitioners sought for enhancement of compensation and after enhancement was made, he has received the compensation at the hands of the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
That being the position, the petitioners cannot now contend that the acquisition proceedings insofar as 10 guntas of land were dropped.

No documents are forthcoming at the hands of the petitioners to show that the acquisition proceedings in respect of the petition schedule property measuring 10 guntas of land was at any - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 point of time given up by the BDA or it was dropped from acquisition in a manner known to law.

The learned Counsel seeks to submit that when admittedly, the acquisition proceedings commenced in the year 1967-1970 and compensation was received by the petitioners'
father several decades ago, the petitioners prayer regarding lapse of the scheme in terms of Section 27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, is required to be dismissed on the ground of delay and laches.

Learned Counsel further submits that since, the State Government admittedly notified the entire 2 acres and 9 guntas of land and paid the compensation in respect of the entire lands, it cannot be contended at the hands of the petitioners that BDA gave up its claim in respect of 10 guntas of land.
Even if such stand is taken, it would be contrary to law and therefore, such a contention should not be accepted.

9. Learned Counsels for respondent No.3 and 4, seek to submit that no fault can be found with the said respondents, since the allotment was made in favour of respondent No.3-society in accordance with law, since the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 lands belonging to the society were acquired by the BDA for formation of outer ring road and in lieu of the acquisition of the lands belonging to respondent No.3- society,
allotment was made by the BDA to an extent of 1493.04 sq.mtrs., which is approximately 14.75 guntas of land, including 10 guntas of land which is the subject matter of the writ petition.
10.

Learned Counsel Shri.Pruthvi Wodeyar, appearing for respondent No.3-society draws the attention of this Court to an order dated 25.03.2014 passed by this Court in W.P.Nos.11615 and 11717-11718/2014, which was a petition filed by respondent No.3-society against the respondent-State Government and BDA.

Learned Counsel submits that respondent No.3-society had approached this Court seeking a declaration that the action of the respondent-BDA in forcibly taking possession of 3 acres and 36 guntas of land for the formation of outer ring road without due process of law, is illegal and without authority of law.

This Court accepted the contention of the respondent No.3-society and directed that if the State - 12 - Shri. Narasimhamurthy N vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130852462/
5 NC: 2023:KHC:29335 Government fails to take any further action in the matter of acquisition and payment of compensation to the respondent No.3-society to an extent of 3 acres and 36 guntas of land, the BDA shall allot the land identified by respondent No.3-society and execute a 'Deed of Conveyance' in favour of respondent No.3-society and consequently, the allotment was made by the BDA in accordance with law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Counsel would therefore submit that no fault can be found either with respondent No.3 or respondent No.4, the purchaser at the hands of respondent No.3-society.
11. Learned Counsel Shri.Yeshu Mishra, appearing for respondent No.4 would support the contentions of the learned Counsel for the respondent-BDA and learned Counsel for respondent No.3-society.

Learned Counsel for respondent No.4 submits that respondent No.4 was not aware of the pendency of the writ petition and admittedly, the respondent No.4 purchased the property from respondent No.3-society under a registered sale deed dated 29.09.2015.
Moreover, it is submitted that initially - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 when the writ petition was filed even respondent No.3- society was not impleaded as a party respondent to these proceedings.

12. Heard the learned Senior Counsel Shri.Suresh S Lokre, appearing for the writ petitioners,
learned Senior Counsel Shri.B.S.Sachin for respondent-BDA, learned Counsel Shri.Pruthvi Wodeyar for respondent No.3-society, learned Counsel Shri.Yashu Mishra, for respondent No.4 and the learned Additional Government Advocate and perused the petition papers.
13.
This Court finds that there is substance in the argument of the learned Senior Counsel, who appears for the petitioners.
It is a settled position of law that when certain facts are admitted before a court of law, such party cannot be permitted to rescind from such admission.

When admittedly,
the written statement was filed at the hands of respondent-BDA in O.S.No.1922/2003, clearly stating that in terms of the mahazar drawn by the authorities, which was marked at Ex.D7,
possession of 10 guntas of land which is the subject matter of this writ - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 petition was not taken for the reasons forthcoming from the mahazar itself and on that ground having got the suit dismissed at the hands of the civil court, the BDA cannot now contend before this Court that it had acquired the entire 2 acres and 9 guntas of land and therefore,
it had the right to take possession of 10 guntas of land also.
Such a contradictory stand taken at the hands of the respondent-BDA in its statement of objections cannot be accepted.
14. The petitioners are not denying the fact that their father received the compensation paid in respect of the entire 2 acres and 9 guntas of land.

However, BDA took a stand before civil court that although 2 acres and 9 guntas of land belonging to Shri.T.Nagappa were notified and acquired and compensation was paid, nevertheless, in terms of the mahazar drawn by the authorities, possession Shri. Narasimhamurthy N vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130852462/
6 of 10 guntas were not taken for the reasons forthcoming from the mahazar itself.

entities.text: Narasimhamurthy N vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, if subsequently action had to be taken by the BDA to take possession of 10 guntas of land, then action in accordance with law was - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 required to be taken by the BDA.

There is no reason forthcoming from the statement of objections filed at the hands of the BDA as to why subsequently, the BDA sought to take possession of 10 guntas of land, which were admittedly not taken in terms of the mahazar at Ex.D7, which was marked in the original suit.
It is not sufficient, if it is stated that possession was taken in accordance with law with the help of the police.

What was required to be stated by the BDA was that why and how it sought to be taken possession of 10 guntas of land in spite of taking a stand before the civil court that it did not take possession of 10 guntas of land for the reasons stated in the mahazar.

It is also essential notice that the mahazar at Ex.D.7 is dated 11.11.1976 and the suit in O.S.
No.1922/2003 was disposed of on 20.08.2009.
If thereafter BDA wanted to take possession, it would be clearly contrary to its mahazar.

15. In the light of the said admitted position, this Court finds that if the petitioners contended that they continued to be in possession of 10 guntas of land and - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 cause of action arose for them to approach this Court only in the year 2014 because of the action to disturb the possession being made somewhere in the month of November,
2014, more particularly, on 07.11.2014, then the petitioners cannot be non-suited on the ground of delay and laches.
It is true that the petitioners have made a prayer seeking a declaration that the scheme has lapsed insofar as the petition schedule property is concerned.
However, as rightly submitted by the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners, this Court need not declare that the scheme has lapsed.

16. It is sufficient if this Court were to hold that the possession of the petitioners insofar the petition schedule property is concerned i.e., 10 guntas of land continues to be in possession of the petitioners and the petitioners could not have been disposed at the hands of the BDA, merely because an allotment was clandestinely made in favour of respondent No.3-society contrary to the stand taken by the BDA before the civil court.
Of course, no fault can be found with respondent No.3-society or - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 respondent No.4, the purchaser.

Nevertheless, this Court is of the considered opinion that the respondent-BDA could not have allotted the petition schedule property in favour respondent No.3-society having regard to the admitted fact that the petitioners continue to be in possession of the petition schedule property and the said position was admitted by the BDA before the civil court.

In that view of the matter, the relief sought for in the writ petition can be moulded and consequently, this Court proceeds to pass the following;
ORDER (i) The writ petition is allowed.

(ii) The respondent-Bangalore Development Authority is hereby directed to cancel the allotment made in favour of respondent No.3-Bangalore Urban Employees House Building & Social Welfare Co-operative Society Ltd., more particularly, the petition schedule property i.e., 10 guntas of land in - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 Sy.No.12/9 of Sarakki Agrahara village, Beguru Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.

entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: (iii) As a consequence, respondent No.3-society will be entitled for allotment of an alternative site.
Accordingly, the respondent-BDA may proceed to allot alternative site in favour of respondent No.3-society.
(iv) Respondent No.3-society shall thereafter convey the lands in favour of respondent No.4.
Ordered accordingly.
Office is hereby directed to return the original documents furnished by the parties, while keeping a photocopy of the same for the file.
Pending I.As., if any, stand disposed of.

(ii) The respondent-Bangalore Development Authority is hereby directed to cancel the allotment made in favour of respondent No.3-Bangalore Urban Employees House Building & Social Welfare Co-operative Society Ltd., more particularly, the petition schedule property i.e., 10 guntas of land in - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:29335 Sy.No.12/9 of Sarakki Agrahara village, Beguru Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.
(iii) As a consequence, respondent No.3-society will be entitled for allotment of an alternative site.
Accordingly, the respondent-BDA may proceed to allot alternative site in favour of respondent No.3-society.
(iv) Respondent No.3-society shall thereafter convey the lands in favour of respondent No.4.
Ordered accordingly.
Office is hereby directed to return the original documents furnished by the parties, while keeping a photocopy of the same for the file.
